findings.title: Role boundaries for sensitive actions are not regression-tested
findings.body: Premise: the new role-separation tests mock both authorization helpers as successful for every non-null user at __tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:94-103, and the guard suite at :114-147 only exercises an unauthenticated caller. → Path: a future change can replace requireAuth()/requireAdmin() on getApplicationDetail, decision actions, donor mutation/export, template/settings actions, or issued-document history with requireCapability(), while keeping the request authenticated. → Verdict: Secretaria would gain full family data or an administrator-only mutation, yet the current suite would pass because it never invokes those actions with a Secretaria identity and a rejecting requireAdmin mock. Add table-driven action-level tests that model Secretaria as allowed only for the intended operational list/document-read calls and assert no DB access for each restricted action.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a Secretaria fixture whose requireAdmin mock rejects and requireCapability mock grants only the enumerated capabilities; cover every public server action in the new access surface.
evidence: Premise: the authenticated fixture resolves both authorization helpers → Path: an admin-only action is changed to a Secretaria-granted capability → Verdict: sensitive data or mutation access can expand while the suite passes.
__tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:94-103 → every authenticated fixture resolves both requireAdmin and requireCapability, so it cannot distinguish their use.
__tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:114-147 → the only exhaustive guard test covers unauthenticated calls.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:96-109 → getApplicationDetail returns full household, financial, and document data behind the admin-only helper.

findings.title: Issued-document protections are covered only in isolation
findings.body: Premise: the new issued-document unit suite calls persistIssuedDocument directly with a fake transaction and only a single sequential latest-version response at __tests__/issued-documents.test.ts:15-27; export tests assert the returned preview PDF but not an issued metadata row or its failure behavior. → Path: removing the persistence call from exportDecision/exportContract, removing the row lock, or allowing Secretaria to obtain an old issued-document URL would leave normal PDF preview tests green. → Verdict: the immutable-final-document contract can regress in production (no auditable artifact, duplicate/racing version allocation, or disclosure of superseded documents) while npm test still passes. Add action-level assertions that successful decision/contract exports persist immutable rows, persistence failure does not report a successful export, Secretaria receives only the current eligible decision/contract, and a DB-backed concurrency test proves the lock/unique-version behavior.
findings.suggestion: Cover the export-to-issued-document boundary and the role-filtered URL/history boundary with non-mocked persistence semantics; retain the narrow cleanup unit test.
evidence: Premise: issued persistence and lock behavior are tested only through isolated mocks → Path: export persistence, concurrency serialization, or role-filtered retrieval regresses → Verdict: immutable documents can be absent, race, or leak while the suite passes.
__tests__/issued-documents.test.ts:15-21 → version allocation is simulated by one mocked findFirst result; the test neither creates concurrent callers nor observes the SQL lock.

__tests__/admin-actions.test.ts:393-475 → exportDecision tests assert rendered content and returned base64, with no assertion that issuedDocuments was inserted or that persistence failure changes the result.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:543-548 and :800-804 → export success now depends on persistIssuedDocument, a behavior not asserted at the action boundary.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:809-836 → current-version filtering and admin-only history have no direct test coverage.

findings.title: A tela de observações não oferece a orientação operacional exigida
findings.body: Premise: a única instrução perto da entrada de observação é o placeholder genérico `Registrar observação interna`. → Path: a Secretaria abre o acompanhamento e registra uma nota; a interface não informa que o registro deve ser conciso e operacional. → Verdict: a experiência não cumpre o requisito explícito de orientar a equipe a registrar somente informação operacional concisa, aumentando a probabilidade de notas com dados sensíveis desnecessários.
findings.suggestion: Inclua uma instrução persistente junto ao campo, por exemplo: “Registre apenas informações operacionais breves; não inclua dados sensíveis desnecessários.”
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:136 renderiza apenas o placeholder genérico `Registrar observação interna` → Path: a Secretaria abre o acompanhamento e registra uma nota sem orientação próxima ao campo → Verdict: a interface não comunica a limitação operacional concisa exigida pela especificação.

Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_prd.md, Core Features / Secretariat Observations exige orientação para informação operacional concisa → Path: a única interface de criação está em app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:136 → Verdict: não há texto de orientação que satisfaça esse requisito.

findings.title: Upload category binding lacks a mismatch regression test
findings.body: Premise: submitApplication's only adversarial document-path case substitutes an applications/ path at __tests__/submit-application.test.ts:222-229. → Path: a caller can retain the pending path shape but put the father's document under rg_mae, use the wrong student index/category, or repeat the same pending path; these are the cases validateDocumentCategories at app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:44-59 is meant to reject. → Verdict: weakening/removing category-to-field binding while keeping the generic pending-path check would pass the current suite and permit a submitted application to associate a required document slot with the wrong uploaded file. Add table-driven mismatch and duplicate-path cases that assert no inserts.
findings.suggestion: Mutate each valid fixture path category one at a time, including a duplicate path, and assert the _form category error before the transaction begins.
evidence: Premise: adversarial submission coverage only rejects a non-pending path → Path: a pending path uses another field's category or repeats an uploaded path → Verdict: wrong document binding can be accepted while the suite passes.
__tests__/submit-application.test.ts:222-229 → the sole server-side path rejection tests only a non-pending prefix.
app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:39-59 → production code additionally enforces exact field category and single-use paths.
__tests__/form-actions.test.ts:73-82 → upload-url category tests exercise issuance allowlisting, not binding submitted paths to their form fields.

findings.title: Remover aluno invalida os uploads já concluídos dos seguintes
findings.body: Premise: `removeStudent` apenas filtra a matriz, enquanto os novos uploads carregam o índice posicional do aluno na categoria (`rg_aluno_${i}` e `certidao_nascimento_${i}`). → Path: uma família adiciona dois alunos, conclui os dois documentos do segundo e remove o primeiro; o segundo passa ao índice 0, mas seus caminhos assinados continuam em `.../rg_aluno_1/...` e `.../certidao_nascimento_1/...`. `submitApplication` então exige as categorias do índice 0 e rejeita a solicitação. → Verdict: documentos obrigatórios corretamente enviados deixam de satisfazer a validação após uma operação normal da UI, sem aviso nem meio de reaproveitá-los. Use uma identidade estável por aluno na categoria/payload, ou impeça/reoriente a remoção quando ela exigiria reenviar anexos.
findings.suggestion: Associe a categoria a um ID estável do aluno mantido no estado do formulário, ou descarte explicitamente os anexos afetados e informe que eles devem ser reenviados antes de permitir prosseguir.
evidence: Premise: app/form/_components/step-2-students.tsx:41-43 apenas filtra a lista e desloca seus índices → Path: os campos em app/form/_components/step-2-students.tsx:186-205 já emitiram caminhos com o índice antigo, mas app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:44-59 compara com o índice novo → Verdict: a submissão rejeita anexos obrigatórios que a UI acabou de aceitar.

Premise: app/form/_components/step-2-students.tsx:186-205 deriva as categorias do índice visual → Path: remover um aluno anterior altera esse índice sem alterar os caminhos já enviados → Verdict: os anexos do aluno remanescente deixam de corresponder à categoria exigida.

Premise: app/form/_actions/form-actions.ts:44-59 exige correspondência exata por índice → Path: um caminho `rg_aluno_1` persiste após o aluno correspondente tornar-se índice 0 → Verdict: a ação devolve erro de categoria em vez de criar a solicitação.

advisories.title: Remove the unrelated Go contract excerpt
advisories.body: The specification is for a TypeScript/Next.js system and already defines the authorization interface in TypeScript. Keeping a second, documentation-only Go shape duplicates the same contract with different names (`Active` versus `ativo`) and creates an unnecessary synchronization point for implementers.
evidence: Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:149-178 defines the executable TypeScript authorization contract, while :207-216 adds a documentation-only Go mirror → Improvement: one authoritative vocabulary prevents drift between `ativo`/`Active` and avoids an irrelevant language artifact → Fix: remove the Go excerpt and its workflow-template-compliance preface.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:17-29 → names `lib/auth/authorization.ts` as the authorization boundary and makes no Go runtime part of the architecture.

advisories.title: Remove the duplicated donor-query paragraph
advisories.body: The same `getDonorPledges` behavior is stated twice consecutively. Removing the duplicate makes the benefactor contract easier to scan without losing any requirement.
evidence: Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:379-380 contains identical `getDonorPledges` sentences → Improvement: eliminates redundant normative prose → Fix: delete one of the two consecutive lines.
git diff 5c90842fe230 -- .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md → both duplicate sentences belong to the owned new-side hunk.

advisories.title: Make the footer visual acceptance check observable
advisories.body: The requirement is visual—no clipping, overlap, or truncation at supported viewports—but the listed test only checks that the text exists in rendered markup. That check cannot distinguish a visible footer from one hidden by overflow or a responsive layout regression, leaving the acceptance criterion ambiguous for implementation and release verification.
evidence: Premise: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_techspec.md:453 requires responsive acceptance at 320, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS-pixel widths, but :580 only requires presence in rendered markup → Improvement: a concrete visual assertion makes the no-clipping criterion reproducible → Fix: specify a browser-level viewport check (or screenshot review) at those widths that verifies the identity text is visible and the footer does not overflow horizontally.
.compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_prd.md:94 and :308 require the full FSSPX name to remain visible without clipping, overlap, or truncation.

advisories.title: Assert the validation path for each required document
advisories.body: The table-driven test only checks that parsing fails. Assert that the issue path matches the document field being removed so a future unrelated validation regression cannot satisfy every table row and obscure which required-document rule broke.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/application-schema.test.ts:154-158 clears one dynamic field and asserts only `success` is false → Improvement: each row will identify its own required-document constraint → Fix: inspect `result.error.issues` and assert that one path equals `field`.
__tests__/application-schema.test.ts:8-59 → `validApplication()` supplies a complete baseline, so each table row can safely assert the path changed by that row.

advisories.title: Factor the repeated final-document persistence sequence
advisories.body: Decision and contract export duplicate the actor resolution, no-actor result, persistence call, and persistence-error mapping. A small internal helper accepting kind, filename, PDF, and localized labels would preserve the same behavior while making future issuance invariants change in one place.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:543-549 resolves an issuer and persists the decision, while :798-804 repeats the same control flow for a contract → Improvement: additions such as audit metadata or error handling cannot diverge between final document kinds → Fix: introduce one internal persistence helper parameterized by kind and caller-facing labels.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:543-549 and :798-804 → both branches call `issuanceActorId`, reject a missing actor, call `persistIssuedDocument`, and translate a catch into an error result.

advisories.title: Centralize the Secretariat-target predicate
advisories.body: Activation and password reset duplicate the same lookup and role-qualified update predicate. Keeping those expressions in two flows makes the invariant easier to weaken in only one operation. Extract a `secretariatUserWhere(id)` helper (and, optionally, a shared target lookup) and use it in both actions.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_actions/staff-actions.ts:49-55 and :65-71 repeat `and(eq(adminUsers.id, id), eq(adminUsers.role, "secretaria"))` for lookup and update → Improvement: the role-safety condition has one maintainable definition → Fix: extract a local predicate helper and reuse it in both management operations.
app/admin/_actions/staff-actions.ts:47-76 → these are the only two target-mutating Secretariat operations and both carry the same duplicated condition.

advisories.title: Expand the new client components into maintainable JSX
advisories.body: The issued-document component now compresses its effect, download handler, conditional rendering, and both document lists into three very long lines. With no configured formatter in package scripts, this makes later changes to loading/error handling or document visibility needlessly difficult to review. Split the state type, effect, handler, and JSX branches across normal blocks before extending this UI.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/_components/issued-documents.tsx:11-13 contains the whole asynchronous load, download behavior, and rendered lists in three lines → Improvement: future edits can isolate a single branch or handler and retain reviewable diffs → Fix: format the component into named, multiline effect/handler/JSX blocks.
package.json:scripts → defines no formatter command, so this layout is not an automatically enforced formatter result.
app/admin/_components/application-observations.tsx:7-9 and app/admin/benfeitores/client.tsx:93-100 → the same compressed component pattern appears in the related new UI.

advisories.title: Give the role-specific donor result a typed boundary
advisories.body: The page uses two unchecked casts to reinterpret the same nullable action result as unrelated client contracts. A later query projection change can therefore compile while silently passing an incomplete record to either client. Export explicit row/result types from the action (or map each branch into a typed DTO) so the role-specific projections are checked at the server/client boundary.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/benfeitores/page.tsx:21 and :23 cast `donors` through `SecretariatDonorPledge[]` and `unknown as DonorPledge[]` → Improvement: TypeScript will detect projection drift for each role-specific client → Fix: define and return typed donor DTOs or explicitly map the query result per branch.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:131-152 → getDonorPledges conditionally selects different column sets but has no declared role-aware return type.

advisories.title: Extract and type the secretariat card state
advisories.body: The new card combines two server-action result shapes as inline state types, casts both results back to those types, and renders the complete details panel in one JSX expression. Give observations and issued documents named shared view-model types, then extract the document and observation sections into small components. This removes unchecked assertions and makes the role-limited interface practical to evolve or test independently.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:103-136 stores inline duplicated result shapes and uses `as typeof notes` / `as typeof documents` before a single-line details tree → Improvement: named contracts and smaller render units make changes to action payloads compiler-visible and localize future UI work → Fix: define exported observation/document view-model types and extract the two details sections.
app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:107-109 → action results are asserted rather than assigned through a typed contract.
app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:136 → the full documents and observations UI is compressed into one JSX expression.

advisories.title: Expose role-specific application result types
advisories.body: The page has to force both branches through assertions, including `unknown`, because `getApplications` returns a role-dependent payload without a discriminant in its type. Return an explicitly discriminated role/result union (or separate read actions) and narrow it before rendering. That keeps the secretariat projection contract checked whenever fields or permissions change.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/page.tsx:20-22 uses `applications as SecretariatApplicationSummary[]` and `applications as unknown as ...ApplicationSummary[]` → Improvement: compile-time checking will detect mismatches between the server projections and their role-specific clients → Fix: model `getApplications` as a discriminated union keyed by staff role, or split its role-specific reads.
app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:61-90 → the action selects different column sets conditionally by the authenticated role.
app/admin/solicitacoes/page.tsx:19-23 → the same role branch is available to perform a typed union narrowing.

advisories.title: Split the user-management handlers and markup into readable units
advisories.body: All three async mutations and the complete user-management UI are packed into four long lines. Split the handlers and JSX into normal blocks (and preferably a row component) so error/state transitions and future accessibility changes can be reviewed and tested without parsing a dense expression.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/usuarios/client.tsx:13-16 contains create, activate/deactivate, reset-password, and both sections of the UI as single-line expressions → Improvement: control flow and state updates become independently readable and testable → Fix: format each handler and extract a `SecretariatUserRow` component.
package.json → the repository has no configured Prettier script/dependency, so this maintainability change is not formatter-owned.

advisories.title: Format the new public page trees into reviewable units
advisories.body: Both newly introduced route components place their complete layout, page copy, and conditional rendering in one physical JSX line. Splitting the markup into normal JSX blocks makes individual sections, accessibility attributes, and future edits readable in diffs and allows the donor transfer panel or form header to be extracted independently when either route evolves.
evidence: Premise: app/seja-um-benfeitor/page.tsx:12 contains the complete page header, transfer instructions, and donor form in one JSX expression; app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx:16 does the same for its header and form/unavailable branch → Improvement: individual sections and control-flow boundaries become locally reviewable and maintainable → Fix: format the route trees into multiline JSX and extract a small transfer-details section if it remains substantial.
package.json → the project provides no Prettier dependency or formatting script, so this readability improvement is not formatter-owned.
git diff 5c90842fe230 -- app/seja-um-benfeitor/page.tsx app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx → both dense route trees were introduced by this change.

advisories.title: Remove the trailing blank line in the change brief
advisories.body: The edited change brief now ends with a blank line, which causes Git's whitespace check to report the file. Removing that final blank line keeps the changed documentation clean in repository-wide whitespace validation.
evidence: Premise: docs/changes/2026-07-27.md:18 is a new blank final line → Improvement: `git diff --check` becomes clean for the edited brief → Fix: remove the final blank line.
git diff --check 5c90842fe230 -- docs/changes/2026-07-27.md → reports `new blank line at EOF` at line 18.

advisories.title: Remova a asserção que mascara a API transacional
advisories.body: A asserção dupla faz `tx` parecer o cliente global, embora só seja usada para acessar o query builder. Consultar a versão diretamente com `tx.select` elimina a fuga de tipos e mantém esta rotina verificável quando a API do Drizzle ou seus mocks mudarem.
evidence: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:20 converte `tx` para `typeof db` via `unknown` → Improvement: preserva a checagem de tipos da transação e reduz o acoplamento desta função à forma do cliente global → Fix: substitua `queryable.query.issuedDocuments.findFirst` por uma consulta `tx.select` que obtenha a maior versão e use `tx.insert` diretamente.
lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:19-39 → toda a leitura e a escrita já ocorrem dentro do callback da transação; o cast serve apenas para contornar a tipagem.

advisories.title: Torne explícita a seleção da versão corrente
advisories.body: A expressão com vírgula dentro de `filter` mistura deduplicação e predicado de retenção. Um laço simples ou uma condição com `if` deixa claro que a primeira versão de cada tipo é a escolhida e evita depender do valor de retorno de `Set.add`.
evidence: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:57-58 usa `!seen.has(...) && (seen.add(...), true)` como predicado → Improvement: torna a regra de seleção da versão corrente legível sem efeito colateral embutido → Fix: percorra os itens ordenados, pule os tipos já vistos e acrescente os restantes a um array de resultado.
lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:51-59 → a consulta é ordenada por versão decrescente, portanto a regra depende de preservar apenas a primeira ocorrência por `kind`.

suppressions.candidate: Concurrent version allocation could race
suppressions.note: The transaction locks the application row with FOR UPDATE before it queries the latest version and inserts the uniquely constrained version.

suppressions.candidate: Existing path-based evidence download accepts a storage path
suppressions.note: This existing action remains Administrator-only through requireAuth; the new issued-document flow takes an ID and does not expose a path to Secretariat users.

suppressions.candidate: Canonical scholarship route does not inherit the legacy form layout
suppressions.note: The canonical route independently preserves force-dynamic, active-year behavior, and a shared SealLogo; no concrete broken flow was established.

suppressions.candidate: Task-list lifecycle statuses may not reflect every worktree change.
suppressions.note: The assignment supplies no authoritative completion tracker beyond this list, and status accuracy depends on workflow state outside the documentation hunk; no bounded documentation correction can be established from this review.

suppressions.candidate: Extract the expanded MOCK_USER object onto multiple lines
suppressions.note: This is formatter-owned presentation without a concrete maintainability benefit.

suppressions.candidate: Change the pending task status based only on source changes
suppressions.note: The task's unchecked acceptance criteria require completion evidence beyond the files owned by this polish cohort.

suppressions.candidate: Dense regular-expression escaping in path validation
suppressions.note: The expression is only instantiated from internally constructed category strings and the helper has a concrete validation purpose; no bounded improvement beyond subjective reformulation survived.

suppressions.candidate: Inactive-account check exposes different login behavior
suppressions.note: The condition returns the existing generic INVALID message, preserving credential-enumeration behavior while enforcing deactivation.

suppressions.candidate: Removed disabled upload interactions need a further change
suppressions.note: The assigned old-side hunk is removal of the disabled branch; the resulting uploader remains fully interactive and the related required fields are enabled.

suppressions.candidate: Replace the static SVG img with next/image
suppressions.note: The asset is a small local SVG with explicit intrinsic dimensions; no inspected behavior or project rule establishes a concrete benefit from adding Next image optimization.

suppressions.candidate: Reformat Drizzle statement-breakpoint SQL layout
suppressions.note: The migration follows the Drizzle-generated statement-breakpoint convention; manual presentation changes would not improve its generated migration contract.

suppressions.candidate: Deduplicate the SealLogo instances in the landing page
suppressions.note: The three instances intentionally have distinct semantic locations and sizes, and no common abstraction has a concrete maintenance benefit beyond an extra wrapper.

suppressions.candidate: Simplificar ou editar manualmente o snapshot de metadados do Drizzle
suppressions.note: O snapshot é artefato gerado da migração; uma alteração manual seria frágil e não é uma melhoria de manutenção acionável.

suppressions.candidate: Reformatar a entrada do journal da migração
suppressions.note: O journal é mantido pelo gerador de migrações e a entrada segue as entradas existentes.

suppressions.candidate: Session-stored role or activity could let a revoked Secretariat account retain access.
suppressions.note: requireStaff resolves the session identity against admin_users for every protected operation and rejects missing/inactive rows before requireAdmin or requireCapability can return.

suppressions.candidate: A Secretariat caller could exchange an arbitrary issued-document ID for a ticket or historical artifact.
suppressions.note: The action resolves the ID server-side, then Secretariat callers must match the role-aware current-document query; that query hides pending applications and contracts for rejected applications. No raw storage path is accepted.

suppressions.candidate: A public caller could create a ticket for a traversal or unapproved upload category.
suppressions.note: The category is fixed-set or numeric-index allowlisted before ticket creation; the eventual submitted paths are independently required to match pending/{uuid}/{category}/{filename}, and storage resolves paths under its configured root.

suppressions.candidate: An Administrator could write or mutate internal observations through a direct Server Action call.
suppressions.note: The action requires the observations:create capability and then explicitly rejects any role other than secretaria; the selected source surface contains only insert/read operations, with no update/delete action.

suppressions.candidate: Role constraint could reject legacy administrator rows during rollout
suppressions.note: The additive nullable role column is backfilled to admin on line 28 before the check constraint and NOT NULL enforcement on lines 29-30, preserving pre-existing accounts and decision references.

suppressions.candidate: New foreign keys could reference tables before their creation
suppressions.note: The two new tables are created before their foreign keys are added, and applications/admin_users are established by 0000_init.sql, which is earlier in the journal.

suppressions.candidate: Migration should fabricate historical issued-document rows
suppressions.note: Task 03 explicitly prohibits backfilling historical generation-only exports as issued documents; this migration creates empty storage metadata tables only.

suppressions.candidate: Generated snapshot may omit the new database constraints
suppressions.note: The generated snapshot records admin_users_role_check and the issued_documents check constraints under checkConstraints; it matches the SQL migration and is not manually maintained source.

suppressions.candidate: Required-document schema could be untested
suppressions.note: The parameterized tests cover each top-level mandatory document group and both required student document groups, so there is no concrete unprotected schema branch.

suppressions.candidate: Authorization capability table could be untested
suppressions.note: The unit tests exercise current database identity, inactive revocation, Secretaria denial of an admin capability, and production bypass denial; the surviving gap is action-to-capability wiring reported above.

suppressions.candidate: Secretariat application and donor projections may expose fields from the full administrator queries.
suppressions.note: The role branch selects explicit operational columns (applications: id/status/school/parent names/contact/decision date and student id/name; donor pledges: the documented operational allowlist) before data reaches the Secretariat components. The full queries run only after the non-secretaria branch.

suppressions.candidate: Secretariat could use an old or ineligible issued-document ID to obtain a final-document ticket.
suppressions.note: getIssuedDocumentUrl resolves the persisted record server-side and, for Secretaria, compares it with getCurrentIssuedDocuments. The latter rejects pending applications and filters rejected applications to decisions, while administrators alone can call history.

suppressions.candidate: Decision and contract reissues may allocate duplicate versions across concurrent calls.
suppressions.note: Each persistence transaction locks the application row before reading the latest version and inserting the new record; the migration also enforces unique (application_id, kind, version). This coordinates both kinds per application and prevents same-kind duplicates.

suppressions.candidate: Public donor-first links and canonical route relocation remain inconsistent across landing-page entry points.
suppressions.note: The primary navigation, hero CTA, benefactor band, and quick-access list point to /seja-um-benfeitor before /solicitar-bolsa; legacy route components contain only permanent redirects to these canonical destinations.

suppressions.candidate: Semântica decorativa/informativa do SealLogo
suppressions.note: O componente oferece `decorative`, alt vazio e aria-hidden para uso decorativo, e alt institucional para uso informativo; isso corresponde ao contrato de logo.

suppressions.candidate: Categorias de uploads em caminho bruto
suppressions.note: A allowlist fixa e o padrão indexado rejeitam categorias desconhecidas e com separadores antes da emissão do ticket; `pathsMatchCategory` também vincula cada campo ao caminho pending correspondente.
